newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says will sell Northwest shares.
newsitem.headline: KLM says will sell Northwest shares.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Wednesday it would sell its shares in Northwest Airlines but would strengthen its operational alliance with the U.S. carrier.
"KLM and its U.S. partner Northwest Airlines have agreed in principle on a far-reaching and long-term commercial and operational alliance," the airlines said in a joint statement.

"The agreement in principle also includes the sale of the entire KLM stake in Northwest to Northwest Airlines Corporation (NWAC). KLM will be paid a minimum of $1.07 billion and a maximum of $1.7 billion," the statement said.
"The agreement clears the way for further strengthening of the partnership, which continues to be very successful for both companies," it added.
KLM's stake of about 19 percent in Northwest will be sold off in four annual tranches from 1997 to 2000.
